To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Students’ approaches to learning are important to consider when teaching engineering courses, 2) Students’ learning approaches can be changed through active learning and problem-based learning, 3) Problem-based and problem-solving learning are important for engineering education, and 4) Students’ approaches of learning and problem solving can be measured by means of student evaluation surveys.

the following factors are important to achieve intended learning outcomes: 1) active learning; 2) problem-based learning; 3) practical application of theory; 4) constructive alignment of learning activities with intended learning outcomes.
students’ learning approaches are important to consider in order to achieve intended learning outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
teaching and learning in electrical and computer science bachelor programmes and how to improve teaching methods in order to enhance learning outcomes.
identifying and understanding the factors that contribute to the effectiveness of teaching and learning in electrical and computer science engineering courses.

how to improve learning outcomes in electrical and computer bachelor programmes, with the aim to increase students’ understanding of the material, improve their problem-solving skills, and develop their ability to apply theory in practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
teaching is a complex task, and the best teaching is always a combination of many different methods, tools and tricks.

teaching at the bachelor level requires the use of a variety of different methods and tools, and that the use of these tools should be adapted to the specific learning goals, the specific students, and the specific course content.
the most important thing is to make the students want to come to the lecture, and to make sure that they are not bored when they are there.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students are not passive recipients of knowledge, but active participants in their learning, and that they should be engaged in their own learning process.
students should be actively engaged in the learning process, and that they should solve real-world problems by applying relevant theory.
students are more likely to learn if they are actively engaged and involved in the learning process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students should be given the opportunity to solve real-world problems in the context of the course, using theory that has been taught in lectures and/or in the laboratory.
students are more likely to learn and retain knowledge when they are actively involved in the learning process and when they can see the relevance of the knowledge for their future career.
the best way to teach is to make the course relevant, to make students want to learn.
